key_insight: A neural network potential trained on DFT data can accurately capture oxygen-vacancy energetics and long-time diffusion in SrTiO3, enabling vacancy transport studies beyond the reach of direct ab initio MD.
engineering_relevance: This provides a fast, first-principles-based modeling route for predicting defect behavior in perovskite oxides relevant to ionic conduction, reliability, and electronic transport design.
method: Trained an NNP on AIMD/DFT reference data for pristine and oxygen-deficient SrTiO3.
Validated the NNP against DFT energies, forces, virials, and vacancy formation energies across supercell sizes.
Used large-scale NNP-MD and Arrhenius analysis to estimate vacancy diffusion and migration enthalpy.
evidence_signal: The NNP reproduces DFT reference properties and yields an oxygen-vacancy migration enthalpy of 0.64 eV, close to the experimental 0.67 eV.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the coverage of the AIMD training set, so rare defect environments or extreme temperatures may require additional reference data.
paper_title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
